problem.text: PR #13 reports conversion of arcee-ai/Virtuoso-Small failing when tokenizer_config.json contains "bos_token": null: Tokenizer.__init__ passes None to id_to_token, producing a TypeError.

reasoning.text: An unspecified model BOS ID alone does not guarantee failure. Resolution first consults tokenizer configuration and otherwise defaults to ID 1; EOS similarly defaults to ID 2. Explicit null or an unresolved token can leave the resolved ID None.

impact.text: The merge's first-parent diff incorporates the same two lookup guards as the PR branch commit, covering both BOS and EOS rather than only the reported BOS case.
async0x42 separately reports that the change fixed the same error while converting ArliAI/QwQ-32B-ArliAI-RpR-v1; this is contributor-reported success, not a locally reproduced conversion.

source_notes.text: PR author oobabooga reports the original failure and presents the change; turboderp's discussion response is an acknowledgment, not a test report.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports a native-extension import failure and an environment workaround. Its traceback does not describe the tokenizer None-ID lookup addressed here.
The earlier PR-branch annotation describes the same absence-preserving lookup change and notes that tokenizer construction is shared beyond conversion.

limitations: No real tokenizers backend, complete tokenizer initialization, model conversion or GPU workload was executed.
The scalar check covers only lookup selection; it does not establish downstream padding or generation behavior when control-token IDs are absent.

claims.text: Tokenizer.__init__ now assigns None directly to bos_token or eos_token when its resolved ID is None. Defined IDs retain the existing extended-vocabulary lookup followed by backend fallback for a missing or falsey mapping. The identity check preserves valid ID zero.

The change preserves absence rather than substituting an arbitrary token. Existing truthiness guards omit absent control-token strings from the extended vocabulary, and encode already checks that BOS/EOS IDs are not None before inserting them. ID resolution and padding fallback remain unchanged.

A standard-library transcription checked 12 combinations of resolved IDs and extended mappings: three None-ID cases avoided lookup, while nine defined-ID cases preserved results and backend-call selection. The backend was a recording stub, not the tokenizers library.

annotation.summary: Merge PR #13's BOS/EOS None guards, preventing absent control-token IDs from reaching backend string lookup.
